title: The Moon: Physical Characteristics
text: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite, orbiting at an average distance of 384,400 km. It has a diameter of about 3,474 km (about one-quarter of Earth's diameter) and a mass about 1.2% of Earth's. The Moon's surface is covered in craters, maria (ancient solidified lava plains), and highlands. It lacks a significant atmosphere, leading to extreme temperature variations between -173°C and +127°C. The Moon's gravitational influence causes Earth's tides. The Moon is thought to have formed about 4.5 billion years ago from debris ejected by a giant impact between proto-Earth and a Mars-sized body called Theia.
